players.note: Arvell Reese has been sensational and continues to chug along as an elite IDP weapon. The LB2 in fppg, Reese recorded four solos and nine assists in Week 10. He is locked in as a top-three option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Will Anderson showed up in Week 10, reeling off two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The superstar pass rusher is up to 10.5 sacks, with three of those sacks coming in his last two games. Continue to treat Anderson as a top-three option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Andrew Van Ginkel showed up in Week 10, tallying three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Now second in the league with 8.5 sacks, AVG continues to prove his elite fit in Brian Flores' scheme. Van Ginkel has been hot, with 4.5 of his 8.5 sacks coming in his last three games. Fire AVG up as a top-15 option for a neutral Week 11 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Quinnen Williams stayed in lava form in Week 10, racking up six solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Williams has been on absolute fire for IDP managers and is locked in as a top-15 option while he is cooking. Quinnen is up to six sacks, with five of them coming in four of his last five games, helping him jump up to DL3 in overall fantasy points and DL4 in fppg. Fire Williams up as a borderline DL1 play for a tasty Week 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

George Karlaftis was back at it in Week 10, tallying two solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Furious George is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, with all of them coming in his last five games (4.5 in the last three). Fire Karlaftis up as a top-20 option as long as he stays cooking. Start the Chiefs edge rusher everywhere.

Jeffery Simmons stayed hot in Week 9, notching three solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Simmons is up to seven sacks on the season, with four of them coming in three of his last four games. The DL5 in fppg, Simmons deserves to be counted as a DL1 option until he starts to cool down.

Maxx Crosby showed out in Week 10, racking up seven solos, one assist, one sack, and four tackles for loss. Crosby started the season slow in the sack department, but has now registered one in each of his last three games. He still isn't back to being a top-five play, but there is no longer any doubt about including him in the DL1 discussion. Start Maxx with confidence for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

Jaelan Phillips stepped up in Week 10, racking up four solos, one assist, one sack, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. Phillips is up to 3.5 sacks, with at least a half sack in four of his five games played. Jaelan is a DL2 option when he is actually on the field, but staying healthy continues to be an issue for the talented edge rusher. Tap Phillips as a top-25 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Chop Robinson was excellent in Week 10, reeling off three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Chop has just five sacks on the season but is heating up with at least one sack in three of his last four games. Tap Robinson as a DL3 with DL2 upside as long as he is cooking. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Nik Bonitto was excellent in Week 9, tallying two solos, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Bonitto is up to 4.5 sacks and should be counted as a top-15 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Mike Green was excellent in Week 10, reeling off four solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Green is suddenly up to 5.5 sacks on the season, with 3.5 of them coming in three of his last four games. The Ravens edge rusher deserves to be part of the top-25 conversation for Week 11. Count him as just that for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Adetomiwa Adebawore stepped up in Week 10, notching one solo, two assists, one fumble recovery, and one touchdown. Adebawore has worked his way into the DT1 conversation and sits at a cool four sacks on the season. The Colts defensive lineman can also be counted as a DL3/4 option during the heavy bye. Start him where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football.

Odafe Oweh was excellent in Week 10, tallying three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The rotational edge rusher is up to five sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his last four games played. Oweh played 74 percent of the snaps in Week 10, his highest ttal since back in Week 1, but should go back down or the 65 percent range in Week 11. Count Odafe as a top-30 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Cincinatti Bengals.

DJ Wonnum stepped up in Week 10, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Wonnum is healthy and no longer has to deal with the threat of ceding snaps to Derrick Moore due to Aidan Hutchinson being lost for the year. Wonnum has a healthy five sacks on the season, but this is his first since back in Week 5. Tap Wonnum as a DL3 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.  Add the Lions edge rusher where needed.

Jadeveon Clowney is set to get another start for the Texans due to Danielle Hunter being ruled out on the short week. Jadeveon was solid in his first start of the season, recording one solo, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended on 76 percent of the snaps. Tap Clowney as a DL3 option where needed.

Ashton Gillotte stepped up in Week 10, tallying two solos, three assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Gillotte has been in impressive form, recording a sack in two straight games to put his season total at three. He remains more of a DL5, but with a heavy bye upon us, he can be considered a DL3/4 depending on your bye week attrition. Start Ashton where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Jonathan Greenard showed up in Week 9, posting one solo, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Greenard, who finally has a sack under his belt and has a favorable schedule down the stretch with Pittsburgh, Arizona, Indianapolis, Seattle, and Houston among others. Count him as a DL3 with DL1 upside for Week 11 and beyond. The Eagles are on bye, so he should be flying far enough under the radar that you can add him for a pittance, especially when we consider his proven DL1 talent and upside on a line that is still dangerous sans Jordan Davis.

Derrick Moore was at it again in Week 10, tallying two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Moore has caught fire for the Lions, recording two sacks in back-to-back games. Moore will be leaned on more heavily with Aidan Hutchinson lost for the year, locking him in as a DL3 option for the rest of the season. Start him with confidence where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

T.J. Parker went off in Week 10, exploding for three solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Parker has started to heat up for the Bills, recording at least one sack in two of his last three games. The rookie edge rusher is up to 3.5 sacks and seems to be finding his footing at the right time for Bills fans and fantasy managers alike. Parker has worked his way into a more even rotation with Bradley Chubb and Greg Rousseau and is now firmly on the DL4 radar. Tap Parker as a DL3/4 option for a tasty Week 11 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Colby Wooden stepped up in Week 10, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack was the second of the season for Wooden, who now has a case to be monitored on the DT3/4 radar for those in 32-team leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

Levi Drake Rodriguez stepped up in Week 10, posting two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. It was the third sack of the season for Levi, but his first since all the way back in Week 1. Rodriguez plays a healthy amount of snaps, which helps keep him on the DT3/4, but his limited sack production keeps him out of the DL mix. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

Shelby Harris stepped up in Week 10, racking up three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Harris has just the one sack on the season and is not yet on the fantasy radar in any format. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

Dalvin Tomlinson had himself a game against the Baltimore Ravens, racking up three solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. The sacks were the first of the season for Dalvin, who is now sitting at 2.5 sacks on the year. Tomlinson had not done much prior to this, but does play enough snaps to be considered a DT who can get some DL depth love in 32-team leagues. With that said, look elsewhere where at all possible for Week 11.

L.J. Collier stepped up in Week 10, tallying three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the second of the season for Collier, who is starting to heat up with a sack in two of his last three games. Tap Collier as a DL4/5 option due to both the heavy bye and the plus Week 11 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Logan Hall was back at it in Week 10, tallying two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Hall played just 41 percent of the snaps, which is right around his season average, and notched his third and fourth sack of the season. Hall has started to heat up, recording three sacks over his last two games. Treat Hall as a DT1 option while he is hot. Start him where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Elijah Garcia showed up in Week 10, notching two solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. It was the second of the season for Garcia, who remains off the fantasy radar, at least for now. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

LT Overton stepped up in Week 10, tallying two solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended on just eight percent of the snaps. The rookie actually saw a season low in snaps due to the return of Jonathan Bullard, but still managed the first sack of his NFL career. The diminished Week 10 role ensures that he stays off the Week 11 radar, but he is worth monitoring in case his role grows with the change of defensive playcallers.
